title: GS21 with the priced y factor on production, exposure = standardized PRODUCTIVITY (gvyz10), three fixed-coupon leverage types (0.158, 0.421, 0.684) with QUARTERLY refinancing opportunities (xi = 1/3) so the coupon per unit capital stays within 3% of the type's
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is a PRODUCT of a hidden type and a within-firm state, so the premium is an interaction the ranks cannot span?
notes: 2026-10-22. gvyzl leaked (refinancing at xi = 1% a month, coupon diluted by 1/g at every investment: realized coupon median 0.17 against set-points 0.16/0.42/0.68); gvyzlx (xi 1, kappa_b 0) did not converge (policy cycle: costless monthly borrowing against new capital). This keeps the issuance cost kappa_b 0.004 and raises the refinancing opportunity to one per quarter, so dilution between resets is ~1.14^(0.2) = 3%.

changes: gs_bv [0.1, 0.1, 0.1] x (gs_bzl 0.0 + gs_bzi 1.0 z~): type x productivity exposure, bv_comp 0.0
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv (gs_bzl + gs_bzi z~) y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).

provenance.source_script_note: proposed 2026-10-08 after the gvy25 footprint diagnosis; solves by variants/klc/solve_gs_vy_klc.sh, ids by verify_gs_vy_klc.sh
